question:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:

Make no bones about it
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "to speak plainly without hesitation". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Make no bones about it"** means to speak openly, plainly, and without hesitation or doubt. (बिना झिझक के सीधे बात करना) • **Example:** She made no bones about telling him exactly what she thought of his behavior. • **Explanation:** This idiom originates from a 15th-century saying that referred to something being easy to swallow, like soup without bones. It evolved to mean expressing something clearly and straightforwardly. (स्पष्ट और सीधे तरीके से अभिव्यक्त करना) • **Example:** He made no bones about his decision to leave the company; he directly informed everyone about it. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: To avoid speaking openly** (खुलकर बात करने से बचना): This means not expressing your true thoughts or feelings clearly. • **Example:** He avoided speaking openly about his plans for the future, leaving everyone confused. • **Option 2: To take a neutral stance** (निष्पक्ष रुख अपनाना): This means not taking sides or expressing support for either side in a situation. • **Example:** During the debate, the judge took a neutral stance and refrained from giving any opinions. • **Option 4: To confuse the audience** (दर्शकों को भ्रमित करना): This refers to creating confusion or misunderstanding in the minds of listeners. • **Example:** The speaker's vague statements confused the audience instead of clarifying the issue. 34:Tcb4, The correct answer is: **Acrid**.
